subtitle: Tracking, nutrition, and the principles behind the plan.

sections.title: How to Know If It's Working
sections.intro: Progress in a recomposition (fat loss + muscle gain) phase is slow and non-linear. Don't rely on the scale — it can stay flat for weeks while body composition improves. Use multiple data points over 2–4 week windows.

items.label: Log every set
items.text: Use the Train tab here (or a notebook). Record exercise, weight, reps, and RIR. Without a log, progressive overload is guesswork.

items.label: RIR (Reps In Reserve)
items.text: Aim for 1–3 RIR on most working sets; 0–1 only on the final set of compounds. Hit the top of the rep range with 2+ RIR? The weight is too light — add load next session.

items.label: Photos & measurements
items.text: Photos front/side/back, same lighting & time, every 2 weeks. Tape: waist (navel), hips (widest), thigh, upper arm, chest — weekly, fasted, AM. Female: track waist-to-hip ratio for glute feedback.

items.label: Body weight
items.text: Daily AM weigh-ins, take the 7-day rolling average. Single-day swings are water/food/hormonal noise. The TREND matters.

items.label: Strength benchmarks (every 4 weeks)
items.text: Test a top set of 5–8 on bench, squat, deadlift, hip thrust (F), barbell row (F), overhead press. Strength up = muscle up, even when the scale doesn't move.

sections.title: Progressive Overload Decision Tree
sections.intro: Each session, check last week's log for the exercise and apply ONE:

items.label: ✓ Top of range, RIR 1–2 → Add load
items.text: Upper body +1–2.5 kg, lower +2.5–5 kg. No micro-plates? Add 1 rep across all sets until the next jump is doable.

items.label: ✓ Middle of range → Add reps
items.text: Same weight, +1 rep per set. Reach the top across all sets, then jump load.

items.label: ⚠ Missed bottom of range ×2 → Deload that lift
items.text: Drop load 10%, rebuild. Often a sleep/nutrition/recovery signal — investigate.

items.label: ⚠ Stalled 2+ wks on multiple lifts → Full deload
items.text: Cut working sets 40–50% and load 10–15% for one week, then resume.

items.label: Weeks 1–4: Adaptation
items.text: Change nothing. Own the movements. Light progression only.

items.label: Weeks 5–8: Progression
items.text: Aggressive load progression. Add 1 set to priority muscles (back/glutes for female) if recovery allows.

items.label: Week 9: Deload
items.text: Mandatory recovery week.

items.label: Weeks 10–16: Phase 2
items.text: Swap variations (barbell row → Pendlay; back squat → front squat; flat → low-incline). Same muscles, fresh stimulus. Keep the Push/Pull structure.

items.label: After 16 weeks → Reassess
items.text: Compare photos/measurements to baseline. Adjust priorities by what lagged. If fat loss plateaus, recalc macros (Nutrition).

sections.title: Recomposition Reality Check
sections.intro: Expect: scale −0.25 to −0.5 kg/week (slower for the female); muscle 0.5–1 kg/month (M), 0.25–0.5 kg/month (F); fat loss visible in 4–6 weeks; strength in 2–3 weeks. If after 4 weeks nothing changed (measurements, photos, strength, scale), there's a calorie/protein gap. If the scale drops >0.7 kg/week and strength falls, calories are too low. Adjust 100–150 kcal at a time.

sections.title: Nutrition Philosophy
sections.intro: Built around chicken and potatoes as protein/carb anchors, with rotating fibre sources. Goal: a modest calorie deficit with high protein to drive recomposition — fat loss while building muscle. Macros are starting points; adjust from the Tracking feedback after 2–3 weeks.

items.label: MALE (30s, ~80–85 kg, moderate activity)
items.text: Calories: ~2,200–2,400 kcal (deficit 300–400) Protein: 170–190 g (≈2.0–2.2 g/kg) — PRIORITY Carbs: 220–250 g (around training) Fat: 65–75 g (≈0.8 g/kg) Fibre: 35–40 g · Water: 3–3.5 L

items.label: FEMALE (30s, ~60–70 kg, moderate activity)
items.text: Calories: ~1,700–1,900 kcal (deficit 250–350) Protein: 130–150 g (≈2.0–2.2 g/kg) — PRIORITY Carbs: 160–190 g (around training) Fat: 55–65 g (≈0.9 g/kg, hormonal health) Fibre: 28–32 g · Water: 2.5–3 L

sections.title: Sample Day — MALE
sections.intro: Chicken & potato anchored. ~2,300 kcal / 180g P / 230g C / 70g F / 38g fibre.

items.label: Breakfast ≈500 kcal
items.text: 3 whole eggs + 2 whites scrambled w/ spinach & tomato · 1 slice wholegrain toast · 1 small apple · black coffee ≈ 40P / 35C / 22F / 7 fibre

items.label: Lunch ≈600 kcal — chicken & potato
items.text: 200g grilled chicken breast · 300g roasted baby potatoes (skin on) · big salad: greens, cucumber, capsicum, ½ avocado, olive oil + lemon · 1 tbsp pumpkin seeds ≈ 55P / 55C / 20F / 11 fibre

items.label: Pre/Intra ≈250 kcal
items.text: Greek yoghurt 200g (0%) + ½ cup oats + 1 tbsp honey + berries ≈ 25P / 40C / 3F / 6 fibre

items.label: Dinner ≈700 kcal — chicken & potato
items.text: 200g chicken thighs (skinless) · 350g baked sweet potato · 200g broccoli + green beans · 1 tsp olive oil · garlic & herbs ≈ 50P / 70C / 18F / 12 fibre

items.label: Evening ≈250 kcal
items.text: 1 scoop whey OR 200g low-fat cottage cheese · 1 kiwi/pear · 20g almonds ≈ 30P / 25C / 12F / 4 fibre

sections.title: Sample Day — FEMALE
sections.intro: Same anchors, smaller portions. ~1,800 kcal / 140g P / 175g C / 60g F / 30g fibre.

items.label: Breakfast ≈400 kcal
items.text: 2 whole eggs + 2 whites scrambled w/ spinach · 1 slice wholegrain toast · ½ avocado · black coffee ≈ 28P / 25C / 20F / 7 fibre

items.label: Lunch ≈450 kcal — chicken & potato
items.text: 150g grilled chicken breast · 200g roasted baby potatoes (skin on) · big salad: greens, cucumber, capsicum, cherry tomatoes, 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon ≈ 42P / 40C / 14F / 8 fibre

items.label: Pre/Intra ≈200 kcal
items.text: Greek yoghurt 150g (0%) + ¼ cup oats + berries ≈ 20P / 25C / 2F / 4 fibre

items.label: Dinner ≈550 kcal — chicken & potato
items.text: 150g chicken thighs (skinless) · 250g baked sweet potato · 200g broccoli + green beans · 1 tsp olive oil · garlic & herbs ≈ 38P / 55C / 15F / 10 fibre

items.label: Evening ≈200 kcal
items.text: 150g low-fat cottage cheese OR 1 scoop whey · 1 kiwi · 10g almonds ≈ 22P / 18C / 8F / 3 fibre

sections.title: Accessible Fibre Sources (Rotate)
sections.intro: Fibre is non-negotiable for satiety in a deficit, gut health, and longevity. Aim for variety:

items.text: Veg: broccoli, spinach, kale, cauliflower, carrots, Brussels sprouts, capsicum, cabbage, zucchini Fruit: berries, apples, pears, kiwi (skin), oranges, bananas (limit if cutting) Grains: oats, wholegrain bread, brown rice, quinoa Legumes: lentils, chickpeas, black/kidney beans Seeds/nuts: chia, flax, pumpkin seeds, almonds, walnuts Potatoes: sweet potato, baby potatoes — KEEP THE SKIN

items.label: Micronutrients
items.text: Vitamin D (1000–2000 IU if indoor), Omega-3 (fatty fish 2×/wk or 1g EPA+DHA), Magnesium (300–400mg, sleep/recovery), Iron (esp. female — leafy greens, red meat 1–2×/wk).

items.label: Sleep
items.text: 7–9 h/night, consistent. The biggest predictor of recovery, hunger hormones, and body comp. Poor sleep wrecks progress faster than any diet error.

items.label: Pre-workout fuelling
items.text: 1.5–2 h before: ~30g protein + 40–60g carbs.

items.label: Refeed / diet break
items.text: Every 6–8 weeks, eat at maintenance 4–7 days. Restores leptin, eases metabolic adaptation. Don't binge — same foods, just more.

items.label: Alcohol
items.text: Counts as 7 kcal/g. >2 drinks blunts protein synthesis ~24h. Keep to rest days, not pre-training.

sections.title: Training Day vs Rest Day
sections.intro: Protein stays identical every day. Carbs and calories flex around training:

items.label: Training days (4u00d7/wk)
items.text: Add 30u201350g carbs vs the base plan, placed in the pre- and post-workout meals (bigger oats serve, extra 100g potato). Calories land at the TOP of your range.

items.label: Rest days (3u00d7/wk)
items.text: Drop 30u201350g carbs (halve the snack oats, smaller potato serve), add a little fat for satiety (extra u00bc avocado or 10g nuts). Calories land at the BOTTOM of your range.

items.label: Why
items.text: Carbs fuel sessions and refill muscle glycogen — centring them on training days improves performance while keeping the weekly deficit intact.

items.label: 4u20135 feedings/day
items.text: 30u201350g protein each (u22480.4u20130.5 g/kg per meal). The sample days already do this — donu2019t skip meals and u201cbanku201d protein into one giant dinner; muscle protein synthesis caps per sitting.

items.label: Pre-sleep protein
items.text: The evening cottage cheese / casein-style serve isnu2019t filler — slow-digesting protein before bed supports overnight muscle repair. Keep it.

items.label: Post-workout
items.text: 30u201350g protein + 60u201390g carbs within ~2h of training. The dinner is built for exactly this.

items.label: Sunday batch (Monu2013Wed)
items.text: Grill/bake 1.5u20132 kg chicken (mix breast + thigh) u00b7 tray-roast 1.5 kg baby potatoes + 1 kg sweet potato u00b7 steam 3 bags of greens u00b7 portion into containers at the cooked weights in your plan.

items.label: Wednesday top-up (Thuu2013Sun)
items.text: Repeat at half size. Salads assembled fresh daily (5 min).

items.label: Rotate sauces, not foods
items.text: Same chicken + potatoes, different week: peri-peri u00b7 lemon-herb u00b7 smoked paprika + garlic yoghurt u00b7 soy-ginger-chilli u00b7 chimichurri u00b7 tikka + mint yoghurt. Sauces run ~30u201360 kcal — log loosely, donu2019t fear them. Boredom kills diets, not sauce.

items.label: Chicken breast u2194
items.text: Turkey breast (1:1) u00b7 white fish like basa/cod (1:1) u00b7 5% lean beef mince (u22480.9:1) u00b7 canned tuna in springwater u00b7 firm tofu (1.5:1 — protein is lower).

items.label: Potatoes u2194
items.text: 300g potato u2248 180g cooked white rice u2248 200g cooked quinoa u2248 180g couscous u2248 2 small wholegrain wraps. Staying with potatoes? Keep the skin.

items.label: Greek yoghurt u2194
items.text: Skyr (1:1) u00b7 cottage cheese (1:1) u00b7 whey mixed in milk.

items.label: Take daily
items.text: Creatine monohydrate 5g — any time, every day, both of you u00b7 Vitamin D 1000u20132000 IU with a fat-containing meal u00b7 Omega-3 ~1g EPA+DHA if not eating fatty fish 2u00d7/wk.

items.label: Use as tools
items.text: Whey — only to close the gap to your protein target u00b7 Caffeine 200u2013300mg 30u201345 min pre-workout, hard cutoff 8h before bed u00b7 Magnesium glycinate 300u2013400mg evenings if sleep is restless.

items.label: Skip — money wasters
items.text: BCAAs (redundant with adequate protein) u00b7 fat burners u00b7 testosterone boosters u00b7 greens powders as a vegetable replacement.

sections.title: When Fat Loss Stalls — Adjustment Ladder
sections.intro: u201cStalledu201d = 2u20133 weeks with no change in 7-day average weight, measurements, or photos. Apply ONE rung at a time, give it 2 weeks:

items.label: 1. Audit first
items.text: Tighten logging for one week — oils, sauces, bites, drinks. Most stalls are tracking drift, not metabolism.

items.label: 2. Add movement
items.text: +2,000 steps/day before cutting any food.

items.label: 3. Trim slightly
items.text: u2212100u2013150 kcal/day from carbs or fat. NEVER cut protein.

items.label: 4. Diet break
items.text: After 10u201312 weeks of dieting, take 1u20132 weeks at maintenance, then resume. This is part of the plan, not failure.

items.label: ð¬ 2× Weekly Frequency
items.text: Training each muscle ≥2×/week beats once-weekly for hypertrophy (Schoenfeld 2016). Push/Pull hits this in 4 sessions — upper + lower trained every gym day.

items.label: ⚖️ Aligned Push & Pull Days
items.text: Both programs share the structure: Day 1 & 3 = Push, Day 2 & 4 = Pull. Train together, each on their own variation.

items.label: ð¦´ Joint-First Selection
items.text: Trap-bar deadlifts (M) for less spinal shear, chest-supported rows, moderate inclines, controlled tempo, mandatory face pulls. Compounds first when freshest.

items.label: ð§ Anti-Imbalance
items.text: Single-leg work every push session; unilateral rows (F) on pull days to prevent dominant-side overdevelopment.

items.label: ð Progressive Overload
items.text: Add 1–2.5 kg upper / 2.5–5 kg lower when you hit the top of the range at 1–2 RIR. Deload every 4–6 weeks (−40–50% volume).

items.label: Warm-Up
items.text: 5 min light cardio + band pull-aparts + bodyweight squats + arm circles. Lubricates joints.

items.label: Tempo
items.text: 3-1-2-0 on most lifts. Cuts momentum-based joint stress, raises time under tension.

items.label: Zone 2 Cardio
items.text: 20–30 min easy cardio (60–70% max HR) on 2–3 rest days. Boosts mitochondrial health (Cell Metabolism 2024).

items.label: Mobility
items.text: 5–10 min post-session: hip 90/90, thoracic rotations, shoulder sleeper stretch, ankle dorsiflexion.

items.label: Deload
items.text: Every 4–6 weeks reduce sets 40–50% and load 10–15%. Tendons adapt 6–10× slower than muscle.

sections.title: ⚠ Shoulder Injury Protocol (Both)
sections.intro: Both have a right-shoulder history that's currently symptom-free. Keep it that way:

items.label: Daily prehab (5 min)
items.text: Band external rotations 2×15, band pull-aparts 2×20, wall slides 2×10 — every gym day before warming up. Insurance, not optional.

items.label: Mandatory modifications
items.text: NEVER: behind-the-neck pulldowns/presses, narrow-grip upright rows, dips below 90°, bench with elbows flared 90°. ALWAYS: face pulls every pull day, lateral raises with slight forward lean & thumbs up, neutral-grip pressing.

items.label: Pain vs discomfort
items.text: Muscle burn = good. Joint pinch / sharp pain / next-day lingering = stop, ice 10 min, swap to a pain-free variation.

items.label: Monthly asymmetry check
items.text: Compare L vs R on single-arm row, single-arm press, lateral raise. >15% gap → reduce the strong side 10% and add 1 set to the weak side until even.

items.label: Warning signs
items.text: Night pain, directional weakness, or painful clicking → get a physio assessment before more pressing/overhead work.

items.label: Steps
items.text: 8,000–10,000/day outside training. The most underrated fat-loss tool — joint-friendly, low cortisol.

items.label: Menstrual cycle (female)
items.text: Strength peaks follicular (post-period→ovulation), dips late luteal (pre-period). Track across full cycles; don't panic at weekly dips.

items.label: Caffeine timing
items.text: 200–400mg pre-workout helps. Cut off 8 h before bed (half-life ~5h) to protect sleep.

items.label: Creatine monohydrate
items.text: 5g/day, any time. Most-researched supplement: ~5% strength, modest hypertrophy, safe. Both should take it.

items.label: Stress & cortisol
items.text: Chronic stress tanks recovery & promotes fat storage. If life is stressful, cut training volume 20% — not the reverse.

items.label: Annual bloodwork
items.text: Baseline: lipids, HbA1c, vitamin D, B12, iron/ferritin, TSH, testosterone (M), CMP. Repeat yearly.

items.label: Footwear
items.text: Flat-soled shoes (Converse, Metcon, lifters, barefoot-style) for squats/deadlifts/hip thrusts. Running shoes compress and kill force transfer.

items.label: Don't program-hop
items.text: Trust the structure 12–16 weeks before judging. Boredom isn't a reason to switch — progress is non-linear.

sections.title: Why Exercises Sit Where They Do

items.label: Leg curls on Pull days
items.text: Hamstrings are knee flexors & hip extensors — both pulling functions — so they pair with deadlifts/rows. Quad isolation would be a push-day item.

items.label: Squats on Push, Deadlifts on Pull
items.text: Squat = knee-dominant push; deadlift = hip-dominant pull. That's why legs split this way instead of a separate day.

items.label: Hip thrusts on Pull (female)
items.text: Hip extension = pulling pattern (glutes/hams contract). Biomechanically belongs with deadlifts.

items.label: Face pulls every Pull day
items.text: Best shoulder prehab there is. The repetition is intentional insurance, not redundancy.

sections.title: Female: Back & Glute Specialisation
sections.intro: Two priorities: back and glutes . Pull A = thickness (deadlift, bent-over row, T-bar row, face pulls, straight-arm pulldown) + heavy barbell hip thrust. Pull B = width (pull-ups/wide pulldown, close-grip pulldown, single-arm row, reverse fly) + single-leg hip thrust & cable pull-through. Push days stay glute-biased (deep squats, long-stride lunges, sumo squats, kickbacks). ~28 back + ~22 glute sets/week — both above the threshold for max hypertrophy. Chest trimmed to ~9 sets to fit the ~65-min window.

sections.title: Day Alignment
sections.intro: Both share the rhythm Push A → Pull A → Rest → Push B → Pull B → Rest → Rest . Same gym days, same movement focus; she loads back & glutes harder on pull days, he runs his own intensity. Shared recovery pattern simplifies scheduling.

sections.title: Lift Intensity Playbook — How Hard Each Lift Should Be
sections.intro: Every exercise in the Plan tab now carries a colour-coded intensity tag. Going 100% on everything every week is the fastest route to a stall or an injury. The system:

items.label: CNS-HEAVY — deadlifts
items.text: The most fatiguing lifts in the program. Top set at RPE 7u20138 (2u20133 reps in reserve), every rep moving with intent. NEVER pull 100% weekly — alternate a heavy week (top set RPE 8) with a moderate week (RPE 6u20137, crisp and fast). Test a true max only every 8u201312 weeks, fresh, early in the session.

items.label: TIER 1 — squat, bench, barbell hip thrust, bent-over row
items.text: RIR 2u20133 most weeks. Only the FINAL set goes to RIR 1, and only in the last week of a wave. Add load once all sets reach the top of the rep range. Grinding these costs days of recovery for no extra growth.

items.label: TIER 2 — DB presses, rows, pulldowns, leg press, lunges, split squats
items.text: RIR 1u20132. Your main growth drivers at lower joint cost — push hard, but the set ends when form changes, not when you collapse.

items.label: ISOLATION — raises, curls, pushdowns, flyes, face pulls, leg curls, glute finishers
items.text: Safe to push to RIR 0u20131; occasional true failure is fine here. Chase the squeeze and the pump. If form breaks, drop the weight ~20% and keep going rather than cheat.

items.label: CORE & CARRIES
items.text: Quality over load, RIR 2+. The set ends the moment position degrades — a sagging plank trains nothing good.

items.label: The 4-week wave
items.text: Wk1: everything at RIR 3 (feels easy — thatu2019s correct). Wk2: RIR 2. Wk3: RIR 1u20132, isolation may touch 0 — the heaviest week. Wk4: start the next wave slightly heavier; every second wave, make Wk4 a deload (u221240u201350% sets, u221210u201315% load).

items.label: Autoregulate
items.text: Slept badly, stressed, or run-down? Keep the session, drop all loads 5u201310%. Showing up at 90% beats skipping — or grinding at 100%.
